name: data-ts-file-editor
description: .ts parser that visualizes the data in a data.ts files so it's easier to edit for non devs

paragraphs: A small Next.js app that turns a data.ts (or .tsx/.js/.jsx) file exporting an array of objects into an editable form UI — so non-developers (or anyone who'd rather not hand-edit TypeScript) can update content and export a file that still looks like it was written by hand.
Upload a file, edit the generated fields, and download the result with the rest of the file — formatting, imports, comments, everything outside the array — left untouched.
features: AST-based parsing — works with real TypeScript syntax, not just JSON
Round-trips key quoting style (quoted vs. unquoted object keys) to match the original file
Non-destructive: only the array contents change, the rest of the file is untouched
No backend, no database — everything happens client-side in the browser
